title: predictive-headroom-controller-for-dedicated-fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated GPU pools must provide predictable throughput guarantees under bursty LLM workloads while avoiding unsafe surge behavior that jeopardizes cluster stability or cross-tenant fairness. Current reactive autoscalers are either too slow (miss SLOs on sudden sustained bursts) or too aggressive (overprovisioning during transient spikes).

Objective: Design and implement a Predictive Headroom Controller (PHC) for Dedicated fleets that combines short-horizon forecasting, configurable headroom targets per-tenant/pool, and conservative safety envelopes. The PHC should be pluggable into the existing scaling orchestrator and support both step and gradual scaling profiles, per-tenant max-concurrency limits, and emergency venting when kernel saturation is detected.

Scope: policy engine (decision logic), metric targets (throughput, token/s, p95 latency, active concurrency), safety limits (max nodes, surge window, cooling period), telemetry hooks, experiment harness, and rollout plan. Does not include hardware procurement or changes to runtime kernels.

Risks: inaccurate forecasts leading to oscillation, complex tuning surface for customers, and potential interplay with dedicated autoscale quotas. Mitigations listed in Implementation Notes below.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes a config schema: target_metric (throughput|latency|concurrency), target_quantile (e.g., p95), headroom_pct (integer), max_replicas, surge_limit and cool_down_seconds
On synthetic burst tests (see Test Plan), PHC maintains configured p95 latency target within +/-10% while using <=20% additional capacity vs baseline predictive target
Safety envelope enforced: no tenant causes >surge_limit additional nodes in a 5m window and all emergency vent events logged with root cause
Observability: per-tenant charts for predicted demand, allocated capacity, headroom buffer, and controller decisions available in Console rollout panel
API compatibility: operator can temporarily disable predictive mode and fall back to conservative step-scaler without changing client routing config
implementation_notes: Forecasting: implement lightweight AR(1)+EWMA hybrid on time-series of 1s and 30s aggregates to predict 30s horizon; keep models per-tenant and per-model-size class

Decision logic: compute desired_capacity = ceil(predicted_qps * (1 + headroom_pct/100) / node_capacity_estimate) then clamp to [min_replicas, max_replicas] and apply rate limiter (max_scale_step, surge_limit) for safety
Safety checks: detect kernel saturation via GPU util and warm-cache miss rates; if saturation observed, throttle surge and trigger fallbacks to cheaper model variants
Fairness: respect tenant_priority_slots—if global capacity constrained, reduce headroom for lower-priority tenants before affecting P0 tenants
Config surface: per-fleet default plus per-tenant overrides; provide safe presets (conservative|balanced|aggressive) documented in Console
Backward compatibility: controller is off by default; enable via fleet config and staged rollout using rollout flags
test_plan: Unit tests for forecast model with synthetic time-series (spikes, ramps, noise)
Integration tests in staging fleet simulating 1k tenants with mixed burst patterns using load-generator harness (github.com/redwood-inference/load-harness PR #234)
Chaos test: random node failures + delayed autoscaler loop to validate cooldown and surge limits
Performance test: ensure controller loop adds <150ms median decision latency and scales decisions remain within rate limits
SLO verification: automated evaluation job that asserts p50/p95 targets under defined scenarios and records cost delta vs baseline
rollout_plan: Alpha: enable PHC on 2 non-production fleets (staging-a/staging-b) for 2 weeks and run canary traffic
Beta: enable on 10 low-risk customer-dedicated pools with monitoring and rollback playbook; invite SEs to validate
Gradual: automated ramp to fleet percentage (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with safety gates based on regression alerts and manual approvals
Rollback: immediate disable predictive mode and revert to step-scales; telemetry will flag recent scaling decisions and PRs linked for postmortem
